body: Parakrama Samudraya Polonnaruwa's Ancient Engineering MarvelThe Parakrama Samudraya, literally translating to "Sea of Parakrama," stands as one of Sri Lanka's most impressive ancient engineering achievements. This vast irrigation reservoir in Polonnaruwa was built by King Parakramabahu I in the 12th century and remains a testament to the advanced hydraulic civilisation of ancient Sri Lanka.Historical SignificanceConstructed during the golden age of Polonnaruwa (1153-1186 AD), this massive tank was part of King Parakramabahu's vision to ensure that "not a single drop of water should flow into the ocean without serving human purpose." The reservoir originally covered approximately 2,500 hectares and was created by damming the Amban River.The king's philosophy of water conservation is immortalised in his famous declaration, showcasing the sophisticated understanding of sustainable agriculture and resource management that existed over 800 years ago.What to See and DoThe Reservoir Itself: The sheer scale of Parakrama Samudraya is breathtaking. Walking along the 14-kilometer bund (embankment) offers spectacular views, particularly during sunrise and sunset when the water mirrors the changing sky colors.Bird watching: The reservoir attracts numerous bird species, making it a paradise for bird enthusiasts. You'll spot painted storks, pelicans, cormorants, and various migratory birds, especially during the dry season.Photography:The picturesque scenery provides excellent photo opportunities. The ancient tank against the backdrop of Polonnaruwa's ruins creates stunning compositions, particularly in the golden hour.Statue of King Parakramabahu:Near the reservoir, you can visit the famous statue believed to be King Parakramabahu I, holding a yoke that symbolizes the burden of kingship.Parakrama Samudraya offers a unique perspective on Sri Lanka's ancient civilization. Unlike the temple ruins and archaeological sites, this working irrigation system demonstrates the practical genius of ancient Lankan kings. It's a place where history, engineering, nature, and tranquility converge, offering visitors a chance to appreciate both the ingenuity of the past and the natural beauty of the present.The reservoir continues to serve its original purpose, irrigating thousands of acres of paddy fields, making it not just a historical monument but a living legacy of sustainable water management.Nearby AttractionsPolonnaruwa Ancient CityRoyal Palace ComplexGal Vihara (Rock Temple)Rankot ViharaLankatilaka TempleTivanka Image HouseVisitors consistently praise the peaceful atmosphere, the impressive scale of the ancient engineering, and the beautiful sunset views. Many recommend renting bicycles to explore the area at a leisurely pace and appreciate that it offers a quieter complement to the busier temple sites.

body: The reservoir was built by King Parakramabahu 1 in an attempt to alleviate water shortages during the dry seasons. There were 5 reservoirs to ease the pressure on the main dam. Thopa Vewa was constructed in 386AD and the King had the other four reservoirs built and the system expanded with many smaller reservoirs to built to feed the five primary and take away any excess water. It was a complex ancient technology that worked until reconstructed in the 19th century when a structural design error altered the water flows. As a result there are now two lakes the largest consisting of Thopa Vewa, Eramudu Vewa and Dumbuthula Vewa and the smaller Kalahagala Vewa and Bhu Vewa. A very scenic area and we had the good fortune to see a small herd of seven elephants nearby.
title: The Sea of King Parakramabahu

body: Parakrama Smudraya-Sea of Parakrama is one of the greatest milestone of Sri It is the Sri Lankan irrigation history. Parakramabahu Great ( 1164-1196 AD) built this reservoir by connecting five nearby lakes during Polonnaruwa era. Latest renovation happened at latter part of colonial era under the guidance of Sir D.S.Senanayaka. There are many things to visit around Parakrama Samudraya. We had an opportunity to have a boat ride at Parakrama Samudraya by fishing boats. It was a half a day journey without life jackets. Better visit this place having the background history knowledge. A very large man made water body to hold & retain water for agricultural purposes built by the ancient Kings. Parakrama Samudra (or King Parakrama's sea or the Sea of King Parakrama) is a shallow reservoir, consisting of three separate reservoirs connected by narrow channels in Polonnaruwa, Sri Lanka. There are plenty of wonderful sights in Sri Lanka relating to their heritage and the Buddhist faith. It is peaceful and very well preserved. You can drive all along the dam for so many miles up to the other end of the lake.Locals call it Parakrama Samudraya meaning "Parakarama Sea" indicating it is quite large compared to thousands other man-made Lakes (Locals call it Weva) in and around Agricultural areas in the country. The same King is famous for saying " I will not allow any bit of Water fallen from the Sky (Rain) to be drained out to Sea without utilising for my public" Irrigation system which is still used today, yes it is a tank, but you would not know it. It circles the city and was used as a defensive border against intruders many years ago. It was an amazing experience to cross different parts of the lake by fishery boats. There are some paid boat tours organized by surrounding hotels at Parakrama Samudraya.You will definitely feel a Sea like atmosphere when tank is fully filled and wonder how such large dams are built during those times (11th Century) without heavy Machinery or technology. Look other side and you will be more surprised to see astonishing Brick and Stone work in ancient Polonnaruwa City thought to be built around same time also using soil dredged to make the lake. It is a great experience in a morning. We drove towards the Angamadilla village and parked in many places to observe the scenic views of the lake. You may even ride in a bike. For a long ride, morning 6-7am is recommended. But for eve, you shall only ride along the main dam as elephants are coming to the rural end. Paddling a local’s made ORUWA in Parakrama Samudraya was a delightful experience we had. This is a rare chance we had. Sitting and watching in-front of the lake at sunset is really wonderful. Do not use liquor since the police are always watch nearby.

body: The 'tank' at Polonnaruwa is huge and beautiful - it's hard to believe that it's a man-made lake. Our guidebook indicates that it goes under the name of 'Topa Wewa (Parakrama Samudra)'.We cycled past it late in the afternoon on our way from the main archeological sites in the north to Potgul Vihara in the south. Although we didn't come across any tourist facilities on the quiet Lake Road, in our opinion, it's still worth taking a few minutes to relax and admire the views.

title: King Parakrama's sea
body: Parākramabāhu I also known as 'Maha Parākramabāhu' was king of Sri Lanka from 1153 to 1186. Samudra Parakrama alos known as Parakrama Samudra is the largest irrigation tank of king Parakramabahu I. Its 5,600 acres of water irrigated an estimated 18,200 acres of paddy land during that time. Samudra in sinhala means sea hence Parakrama Samudra means King Parakrama's sea.

title: Great man made lake
body: This has to qualify as one of the most far seeing constructions in Asia. The king (seen to be almost as a god by his people) built this lake/reservoir as part of a complex and sophisticated irrigation system which led to great prosperity for his country.Perhaps it has ultimately helped to make Sri Lanka so different to its much larger neighbour even today?
